verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The change correctly publishes a generator-owned, unconditional queue refusal count, keeps it distinct from the surviving-row total, and renders partial or total loss without treating legacy or malformed counts as evidence of loss. Queue-depth trend samples become unknown whenever any queue row was refused. The executed page tests cover empty, fully dropped, partly dropped, legacy, malformed, and forged-count cases, while the generator tests independently pin accepted, refused, capped-warning, and collector-supplied inputs. I found no correctness, soundness, test-vacuity, or security issue in the diff.
